newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai nickel imports seen up this year, zinc down.
newsitem.headline: Thai nickel imports seen up this year, zinc down.

text.p: Thailand's base metal imports in 1997 are expected to post steady growth with nickel demand likely to see substantial growth, industry ministry sources said on Wednesday.
However, demand for zinc ingots was likely to drop as more local production was expected this year, they told Reuters.

"The ministry has not come up with the official forecast for the 1997 but based on the current economic situation, it is our view that base metal demand should rise at a steady pace," a senior official said.
They noted that with the expansion of stainless steel production by Thainox Steel coming on stream in the second quarter of this year, the demand for nickel was set to rise.
Thainox Steel recently expanded annual capacity to 160,000 tonnes from 60,000 tonnes. The new capacity will come on stream by May 1997.
Thailand's estimated nickel imports for 1996 were 2,189 tonnes, up 27 percent from 1,717 in 1995.
Aluminium imports in 1996 were estimated at 290,057 tonnes and copper at 229,565 tonnes, up 14 and 48 percent respectively from 1995.
The 1996 import of lead, used in the battery industry, was projected at 69,281 tonnes compared with 43,785 tonnes in 1995.
But zinc ingot imports last year dropped to 52,712 tonnes from 53,978 tonnes in the previous year.
"The import of zinc ingots is expected to drop further in 1997 as we can produce more locally," said a ministry official.
Padaeng Industry Plc, Thailand's only zinc smelter, will raise its annual output to 105,000 tonnes this year from 73,800 tonnes previously. The expansion is expected to reach full capacity by March.
